title: National Commission's Review of Its Own Orders

content.scenario: A party files an application with the National Commission to review an order passed by it, citing an error apparent on the face of the record. The application is filed within thirty days of the order.
content.outcome: The National Commission shall review the order if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either on its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order.

user_queries: Can the National Commission review its own orders?
What are the grounds for review of an order by the National Commission?
How long does a party have to apply for a review of an order?
